overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the January 15 notice was sufficient on its face, and both the litigation (Purpose 3) and complaint-review (Purpose 1) executive session purposes were proper.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice for the January 15 joint Board and Board of Health meeting was not sufficiently specific about executive session topics.
allegations.key_passage: We find that, on its face, the notice for the January 15 meeting met the statutory requirements.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the executive session exemptions were incorrectly applied; the Board convened under Purpose 3 to discuss litigation strategy with a contractor and engineer.
allegations.key_passage: Here, litigation is pending between the town and Maverick Construction and the Chair declared that public discussion of the litigation would compromise the litigating position of the Board; thus, discussions of litigation strategy were appropriate for executive session.

allegations.summary: Board convened under Purpose 1 to discuss two open meeting law complaints filed by the complainant, which the complaint also challenged as an improper executive session basis.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, our office has unequivocally stated in past determinations that public bodies may meet in executive session under Purpose 1 to review Open Meeting Law complaints against the body.
